class.name: MultiplayerTree
class.brief_description: The node one session's branch is rooted at.

method.name: dispose
method.description: Clears the service registry and the roster, breaking the reference cycles a session accumulates so a torn-down branch can be freed. Called for you when the tree leaves the [SceneTree] for good. Call it directly only when a rig tears a session down without freeing its node.

method.name: raise_embedded_server
method.description: Duplicates this tree as a [constant NetwMultiplayer.ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER] sibling named [code]Server[/code] and adds it beside this one. Node work only. The sibling is raised with [member auto_host_headless] cleared and returned, and bringing it online is an ordinary peer assignment on its own [member api], which is what keeps one bring-up from being written twice. Returns [code]null[/code] when this tree has no parent to add a sibling to. The sibling is freed when this tree's session ends. [codeblock] var server := tree.raise_embedded_server() var peer := ENetMultiplayerPeer.new() peer.create_server(21253) server.api.multiplayer_peer = peer [/codeblock]

members.member: The [NetwMultiplayer] this tree owns and installs on its branch. Built once when the tree is constructed and never replaced, so a reference taken from it stays valid for the tree's whole life. A backend bringing its own transport swaps [member NetwMultiplayer.inner] rather than this. A tree whose installed API is not a [NetwMultiplayer] is unrepresentable.

An optional [NetwMultiplayer] implementation script, passed to [method NetwMultiplayer.make]. The one door a game replaces this session's stages through. Immutable once the tree is inside the [SceneTree], so assign it before adding a programmatically created tree.

A game-build tag that gates admission, baked into every build. A joining peer whose tag differs is rejected during the auth handshake before it reaches [method MultiplayerAPI.get_peers], so an incompatible build never corrupts a session. The tag folds this name together with the wire identity the build speaks, so no value turns the gate off: leaving this empty still rejects a peer whose format version or channel table differs, and naming it adds the game's own compatibility on top. Bump it when the game's own payloads break in a way the wire identity cannot see. This export is part of the tree's session FALLBACK, not a live setting. It is immutable once the session has consumed its configuration. The tag also scopes room codes for signaled transports. Builds with different tags do not share rendezvous rooms. Changing the tag invalidates room codes created with the previous value.

On a headless build, hosts from [member peer_class] and [member transport_settings] without waiting to be asked. Only a [constant NetwMultiplayer.ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] or [constant NetwMultiplayer.ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER] tree does this, and only one naming a [member peer_class], so a tree nobody configured never opens a socket on its own.

An auto-connect applied on play, in debug builds only. When set, the tree hosts on ready under the username and join arguments it carries, skipping the server browser. A release build strips this path because [method OS.has_feature] returns [code]false[/code] for [code]"debug"[/code], which is also what keeps [member link_conditions] free of a release cost.

The [enum NetwMultiplayer.Role] this tree intends to play, carried in the tree's session fallback as [member NetwSessionConfig.desired_role]. Configured intent rather than live state: the role a session is actually running is [member NetwMultiplayer.role], and it is assigned when the session comes online.

Latency and loss to simulate on this tree's peer. Carried in the tree's session fallback as [member NetwSessionConfig.link_conditions], which is the one home the session reads when it wraps an assigned peer. A release export never wraps at all, because [method NetwLinkConditions.wrap_peer] gates the impairment itself, so authoring one here carries no shipped cost.

The class of peer this tree brings itself up with, such as [code]&"ENetMultiplayerPeer"[/code]. Passed to [method NetwConnectHandle.create_peer], so a tree naming no peer class has nothing to bring itself up with and reports a configuration warning. Read [method NetwConnectHandle.transports] for the names a running build has registered. It does not constrain a peer the game assigns itself.

The settings [member peer_class]'s transport is created with, such as [code]{ port = 21253 }[/code] for an ENet server. Passed to [method NetwConnectHandle.create_peer] beside [member peer_class], and carried as the advert, so the [code]name[/code], [code]max_players[/code] and [code]visibility[/code] keys ride here alongside the transport's own. Read the [code]host_settings[/code] entry of [method NetwConnectHandle.transport] for the keys a given peer class accepts.
